samples.summary: `applyListLevelChanges` is copy-pasted into three editors instead of being shared
samples.evidence: The shared piece extracted into `model/list-level.ts` is only the *planner*. The apply half — iterate `changes`, call `doc.setBlockType(id, 'list-item', { listKind, listLevel })` — is written out three times, near-identically: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1601`, `packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:822`, `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2722`, each with its own copy of the same ~15-line doc comment. `siblingsOf` is likewise duplicated between `editor.ts:1637` and `text-editor.ts:2887` with the same cell-lookup logic. All three operate on the same `Doc` type, so a single `applyListLevelChanges(doc, delta, walker, onWritten?)` in `model/list-level.ts` (with the editor-specific `markDirty` passed as a callback) would have covered all of them. The repo's stated expectation is reuse; three copies of the write loop is where the next divergence (e.g. only editor.ts remembers to mark carried children dirty) will come from. Cost stays inside the codebase, hence minor.

samples.summary: Design doc says out-of-band levels are read as-is, but the code normalizes and writes them back repaired
samples.evidence: docs.md states: "Levels that are *already* inconsistent (a level-3 item directly under a level-0 one) are read as-is rather than normalized; the gesture preserves whatever relative depth it finds." The implementation's `levelOf()` (`packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:29-33`) does the opposite for out-of-band values: it floors, clamps to `[0, MAX_LIST_LEVEL]`, and maps non-finite to 0, and `planSiblingGroup` writes `levelOf(block) + delta` — so an item stored at level 48 is silently rewritten to 7 by an outdent, and a `NaN` level to 1 by an indent (the tests at `test/model/list-level.test.ts:141-150` assert exactly this). That repair behavior is a real data-model decision and is not recorded in the canonical subsystem doc, while the sentence that is there reads as its negation. Documentation-only cost, so minor.

samples.summary: Unrelated header/footer fixes to the shared selection walker folded into a list-level change, unmentioned in the design doc
samples.evidence: Beyond the #1050 subtree behavior, the diff changes the shared `forEachBlockInSelection` walkers in ways that affect every other command routed through them: `text-editor.ts` multi-block branch now reads `this.doc.getContextBlocks()` instead of `this.doc.document.blocks` (line ~2857), and `editor.ts`'s cursor-only branch now resolves `cellInfo` from `doc.blockParentMap` instead of `layout.blockParentMap` (line ~1729), changing which top-level block gets `markDirty` for header/footer carets. Other callers of these walkers (`editor.ts:3416`, `editor.ts:3577`, `text-box-editor.ts:1110/1148`, `text-editor.ts:2766/2783` — block style, spacing, margin commands) inherit the new behavior. These look like genuine bug fixes, but they are separate defects from the issue under review, ride along with no test naming them as such beyond the list case, and the docs.md addition describes only the subtree rule. Scope creep in a shared helper; behavior appears improved, so minor.

samples.summary: Design doc's writer count is wrong: says "six writers", enumerates seven
samples.evidence: "All six writers route through it (`handleTab`, `handleIndent`, `handleOutdent` in `text-editor.ts`, and the `indent` / `outdent` API pair in both `editor.ts` and `text-box-editor.ts` ...)" — that enumeration is 3 + 2 + 2 = 7 call sites, all of which exist in the diff. Cosmetic doc inaccuracy.

samples.summary: Each indent/outdent gesture walks the selection twice
samples.evidence: `indent()`/`outdent()` now call `applyListLevelChanges(delta)` (which runs `forEachBlockInSelection` inside `planListLevelChanges`) and then a second `forEachBlockInSelection` for the non-list `marginLeft` branch. Same shape in `text-box-editor.ts:1170-1198` and `text-editor.ts:2763-2790`. In `editor.ts` the walker also calls `markDirty` as a side effect, so that runs twice too. A single walk producing both the list plan and the paragraph list would be one pass; harmless as written, hence a nit.
